data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 collapses the problem's distinction into a single-axis framing. The problem asks to identify what EVIDENCE would distinguish failures that are truly independent from those that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. But SRC_001's entire mechanism rests on whether the topology 'contains verifiable causal firebreaks' — a static structural property. Static topology inspection cannot, by itself, distinguish a genuinely independent failure process from one that is merely quiescent because the shared trigger has not yet occurred: a network with causal firebreaks against known propagation paths can still harbor an as-yet-unenumerated shared cause (common library vulnerability, upstream provider) that jumps the firebreak. By treating firebreak presence as the distinguishing evidence, SRC_001 begs the question — it assumes the shared-cause channel is already known and topologically blocked, which is precisely what the problem asks one to evidentially establish. The third countercondition ('necessary but not sufficient, some other factor dominates') gestures at this gap but never supplies the covering principle that would make firebreaks sufficient for the independence judgment, so the answer under-specifies the very evidence criterion the problem demands.
